answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded, cross-audited registry. Each joining agent posts stake that is slashed when its answers diverge from independent peers, and each epoch it publishes a signed beacon of the jobs it claims. Peers audit those claims through a rotating spiral of reviewers from unrelated operators, so a fake-identity farm must keep real work flowing under every clone at once, paying stake, compute and grading per head. Duplicating one honest operator costs several stakes while payouts stay flat per identity. Weight follows a prism of independent attestations, not registered keys.
